title: Is 30% of TSMC's Advanced Chip Capacity in the U.S. Enough? Former Chairman Mark Liu Weighs In
gist: Forum teaser (posted by karin623) for a TechTaiwan newsletter piece on former TSMC Chairman Mark Liu's first public appearance since retiring: he argues 30% of TSMC's advanced capacity in the U.S. may be enough, discusses why TSMC beat Intel, Taiwan memory's 'three butchers', and reveals Eric Schmidt is making military drones in Taiwan. Body is a summary with no detailed arguments.

themes.theme: TSMC US capacity and silicon shield

insights.claim: Former TSMC Chairman Mark Liu argues that placing 30% of TSMC's advanced chip capacity in the U.S. may be enough, and that something else matters even more.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Signals an insider view that US reshoring targets near 30% may cap further pressure on TSMC to relocate leading-edge capacity from Taiwan.
insights.quote: Why 30% of TSMC's advanced chip capacity in the U.S. may be enough—and what matters even more.

insights.claim: Mark Liu, speaking publicly in Taiwan for the first time since retiring two years ago, addressed TSMC's silicon shield and the future of the global chip industry.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Silicon-shield framing from a former chairman is relevant to Taiwan geopolitical risk pricing.

insights.claim: Mark Liu discussed what he sees as the secret behind TSMC's competitive victory over Intel in foundry manufacturing.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Insider explanation of TSMC's moat is relevant to judging Intel Foundry's catch-up odds.
insights.quote: The secret behind TSMC's victory over Intel.

insights.claim: Mark Liu warned that Taiwan's memory chip industry now faces 'three butchers', implying severe competitive pressure on Taiwanese memory makers.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Bearish signal for Taiwanese memory makers versus larger global rivals.
insights.quote: Why Taiwan's memory industry now faces “three butchers.”

insights.claim: According to Mark Liu, former Google CEO Eric Schmidt is now manufacturing military drones in Taiwan.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Points to Western defense-tech capital building drone production inside Taiwan's supply chain.
insights.quote: Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt is now manufacturing military drones in Taiwan.
